name: setsockopt
synopsis: int setsockopt(int sockfd, int level, int optname, const void *optval, socklen_t optlen);
description: setsockopt() manipulates options for the socket referred to by the file descriptor sockfd. It allows setting options at various protocol levels by specifying the level and option name. The option value is provided via a buffer.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: The file descriptor of the socket.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The protocol level at which the option resides (e.g., SOL_SOCKET).

parameters.name: optname
parameters.description: The name of the option to set.

parameters.name: optval
parameters.description: A pointer to the buffer containing the option value.

parameters.name: optlen
parameters.description: The length of the option value in the buffer.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The argument sockfd is not a valid file descriptor.
The address pointed to by optval is not in a valid part of the process address space.
optlen is invalid, or there is an invalid value in optval.
The option is unknown at the level indicated.
The file descriptor sockfd does not refer to a socket.

bugs: Several of the socket options should be handled at lower levels of the system.
